prompt.en: Which word is a personal pronoun?

stages.choice_rule: Four whole words copied from the stem. Exactly one choice is a personal pronoun from this closed set: I, me, you, he, him, she, her, it, we, us, they, them. The other three are nouns, verbs, adjectives, articles, or possessives (my, your, his, its, our, their). Prefer stems with exactly one personal pronoun. Never put two personal pronouns in the same choice set. her is the key only as an object (Dad hugs her), never as a possessive (her dog). his is never the key. Do not use mine, yours, hers, ours, or theirs as the key.

roots: Keep four unique whole-word choices. Never change the closed key set: I, me, you, he, him, she, her, it, we, us, they, them.
Exactly one personal pronoun may appear among the four choices. Prefer stems that contain only that one personal pronoun.
Wrong choices must be other words from the same stem: nouns, verbs, adjectives, articles, or possessives. Never invent a word that is not in the stem.
Tier 1 keys are subject pronouns I, he, she, we, or they at the start. Distractors are obvious nouns, verbs, colors, or articles.
Tier 2 keys are often object pronouns me, him, her, us, them, or you inside a five-to-seven-word kid sentence. Family nouns and two-syllable nouns are good distractors.
Tier 3 must include a near-miss possessive my, your, his, its, our, or their in the choices. her is the key only after an action. his is never the key.
Never use a real name in the stem. Use <NAME> when a person is needed. A name is never a choice and never the answer.
Stay in kid world: school, home, food, pets, play, family, weather. No brands, no metalanguage in the stem.

tier_rules.1: Short stems of four to six words. The key is I, he, she, we, or they at the start. Distractors are clear nouns, verbs, colors, or articles.
tier_rules.2: Five to seven word stems. The key is often me, him, her, us, them, or you. Use family nouns and two-syllable kid nouns as distractors.
tier_rules.3: Near misses. Put a possessive my, your, his, its, our, or their next to a true personal pronoun. Use it with <NAME>, or her only as an object.

subject_pronoun.en: I, you, he, she, it, we, and they take the place of a name.
subject_pronoun.ko: I, you, he, she, it, we, they는 이름 대신 쓰는 말입니다.

object_pronoun.en: Me, him, her, us, and them come after the action.
object_pronoun.ko: me, him, her, us, them은 동작 뒤에 오는 인칭대명사입니다.

object_not_possessive.en: Her and them stand for people. My and their tell who owns something.
object_not_possessive.ko: her와 them은 사람을 가리킵니다. my와 their는 누구의 것인지 말합니다.

it_pronoun.en: It is a personal pronoun. It stands for a thing, not a name.
it_pronoun.ko: it은 인칭대명사입니다. 이름이 아니라 사물을 가리킵니다.
